style.description:
The language specified in the fenced code block #info. Note that this can be the formal name of the language
("Python") or a standard abbreviation ("py"). The name is case insensitive ("python", "Py").

{@link ImplLanguage Programming languages} will have syntax highlithing support, as will some structured data
languages such as JSON.

spans.description: The spans within the simple block.

blocks.description: The sub-blocks within the compound block.

title:
A Markdown fenced code block, usually with a language associated:

````md
```js
2 + 2
```
````

The language may be the formal name, such as "JavaScript" or a common alias as above. It is also case-insensitive.

Syntax highlighting will be done for {@link DocumentationExample.Language known languages}.

This is also used for indented code blocks (4+ leading spaces), although with no language associated there will
be no syntax highlighting.

This parsed structure appears in the {@link Documentation#description description}. Fenced code blocks within
`@example` annotations are parsed as {@link Documentation#examples separate examples}.
name: DocumentationCodeBlock
